newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf rig crews may have to ride Danny out.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf rig crews may have to ride Danny out.

text.p: Crews remaining on Gulf of Mexico offshore rigs may be left to ride out Tropical Storm Danny as the surging storm threatened to ground helicopter crews onshore, officials said on Thursday.
"We're starting to get calls to pull non-essential (workers) off platforms," a Petroleum Helicopters Inc dispatcher in Houma, La., said. "Our problem is with the rain, it's hard to get out there."
"We're definitely having some problems getting out there," a dispatcher with Air Logistics in New Iberia, La., said.

The slow-moving storm flared up Thursday as it approached the Louisiana coastline, with maximum sustained winds approaching 60 miles an hour and rain bands reaching New Orleans 115 miles to the northeast.

The approaching storm forced the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port to evacuate non-essential workers from its idle offshore platform about 20 miles south of Grand Isle, La., and could delay a 900,000 barrel cargo due on Friday, a dispatcher said.
But the LOOP, the Gulf's only offshore oil port, continued to operate its onshore crude oil pipeline and distribution system, a spokesman said.

The National Hurricane Center in Miami at noon EDT said the storm's center reformed to the northeast, and was centered near latitude 28.6 north, longitude 90.9 west and moving northeast at about 5 miles an hour.
